scope: Qwen3.8 27B UD-Q4_K_XL / UD-Q8_K_XL; Q4_K_M, Q8_0 and BF16 DFlash2 drafts; C1 and fixed seven proposals. Short development probes, not a depth/capability sweep or a controller comparison.
retained: Stream BF16 weights for decode and the large context feature projection. Cache the repeated B16/M1024/K5120 K/V projection; choose the kernel specialization at host dispatch.
Symmetric K-quant/IQ projections omit affine activation sums and offset scratch. A scoped clang fp contract(off) keeps the scaled dot rounded before accumulation; original dot-product FMAs remain.

Remove unreachable verification precision and LM-head settings, their setter and dead prefill branches. Qwen speculative disk-cache identity now records decode-equivalent-v1 and invalidates the previous identity.

The existing GEMM benchmark models matrix reuse for batch-16 injection and applies its production cache hint. Decode ablations rotate at least 128 MiB of weights. No new benchmark executable, test executable or production environment switch.
model_artifacts_reference: dflash2-rollback.json: artifacts (same model files and hashes)

quality.target_scope: After the symmetric arithmetic change: 48 verifier full-logit rows match scalar decode; snapshots/rejected-prefix replay, mixed 32/64-capacity batches and logical context 262144 pass. The final change only specializes BF16 injection cache hints; scalar/verification arithmetic is unchanged.
operators: qwen_q4kxl_quant_ops_test: all supported formats against scalar/reference controls after symmetric rounding change
qwen_gpu_ops_test: BF16 widths 1 through 8 and 16 bit-exact with scalar decode; rerun after final dispatch specialization
quality.final_serving: inference_backend_gpu_test with Q4 target and Q4 draft: direct/served parity, seeded sampling, bounded prefill, cache forks and persistent restore, concurrency, cancellation and reclamation pass.
quality.chat: All 24 cases in the two-repetition projection comparison, all 12 cases in the runtime-cache checkpoint control, and all four final dispatch controls preserve all 128 qualified AR token IDs. All three draft traces remain byte-identical (90 each).
quality.upstream_reference: The unchanged 270 traces are the pinned upstream-qualified references documented in README.md; this preserves that qualification.
quality.remaining: Original target/checkpoint-conversion and MTP qualification, capability/deeper-context refresh, controller comparison and complete C>1 qualification remain open.

speed.interpretation: Gains are small: the two-repetition chat probe shows Q4 +0.5 to +0.7% and Q8 +0.2 to +0.4%. Final Q4-draft controls show +0.42% / +0.25%. pp2048 is within observed run variation; do not claim an end-to-end prefill speedup. Component gains from different workloads are not additive.

two_repetition_projection_comparison.workload: cpp_ring_buffer chat, 128 generated tokens, fixed seven proposals, two interleaved repetitions; timing includes prompt processing. Short development probe, not a full corpus or depth sweep.

final_dispatch_chat_control.workload: cpp_ring_buffer chat, 128 generated tokens, fixed seven proposals, one paired repetition for both targets with Q4 draft after specializing the injection cache hint; timing includes prompt processing. Short development probe, not a full corpus or depth sweep.

final_dispatch_prefill_control.workload: C1 DFlash2 Q4 draft prefill-only, pp2048, 3 timed repetitions after warmup. Includes target feature capture and context injection. Baseline before candidate on both targets, reversing the first prefill control. No depth sweep.

speed.scope_note: The broad chat comparison precedes the final B16 cache-hint specialization. Final controls cover both targets with Q4 draft, and all three drafts repeat full trace/state qualification. Prefill uses pp2048, three timed repetitions after warmup; generation probes use one chat prompt and 128 tokens.

prefill_profile.workload: Q8 target, Q4 draft, pp2048/n0/r1. Totals include warmup plus the timed prefill: 256 feature projection calls and 2560 K/V calls. Profile durations are diagnostics, not throughput estimates.

prefill_profile.finding: Streaming every B16 projection raised repeated K/V time from 131.33 to 220.22 ms. A uniform GPU-loop branch also slowed the large feature projection to 464.25 ms. Dispatch specialization restores K/V to 133.24 ms and reduces the large projection from 362.82 to 341.65 ms.

generation_profiles.finding: Affected IQ4_XS target kernels improve about 3 to 4%; BF16 target kernels about 2%. Some shapes vary or regress, so retention is based on the complete qualified workload, not summing the largest kernel wins.

microbenchmarks.builder: nix develop -c tools/bench/build.sh <probe.hip>; HIP -O3 gfx1151, FP32 activations, bit comparisons before timing.
microbenchmarks.scope: Four alternating geometry rounds. Streaming/ordered-symmetric probes compare the old production kernel with a temporary candidate. Final dispatch ablations compare production batch8 chunks and batch16 injection, with repeated weights; that comparison is not a new gain over the prior batch16 implementation.

rejected: Q8/BF16 token-slab staging: exact, but increased register pressure; Q8 remained 15 to 60% slower after occupancy constraints, BF16 neutral/slower.
Q8 non-temporal weights: exact but neutral. K-quant streaming: Q5 about 8% slower and IQ4 about 30% slower.
Paired gate/up fusion: Q8 gain only about 0.5%; BF16 loses against the retained row geometry. No fused route retained.
Removing the symmetric offset with ordinary/HIP rounding intrinsics permits contraction and changed 94795 of 139264 outputs. Only the scoped non-contracting epilogue is retained.
Streaming reused B16 K/V weights and selecting the cache hint with a runtime GPU-loop branch both regress prefill. Both are replaced by host-selected cache specializations.
